_fonte: Myprotein expands functional beverage offering - Inside Food & Drink Skip to content Latest Edition Company Brochures Company Brochures Brochure Archive News Events Latest Edition Company Brochures Company Brochures Brochure Archive News Events About Media Pack Subscribe Other Publications Contact Us Linkedin Envelope Phone-alt Home Magazine Brochures News Events About Media Pack Subscribe Other Publications Contact Us Linkedin Envelope Phone-alt Myprotein expands functional beverage offering Myprotein has expanded its product portfolio with the launch of Protein Iced Coffee, marking the brand’s entry into the growing protein coffee category with its first product to combine real coffee and protein in a single format. Available in five flavours — Iced Latte, Caramel Latte, Vanilla Latte, Mocha and Matcha — the new range is designed to meet rising consumer demand for convenient, functional products that support both energy and nutrition needs. Each serving delivers 20g of protein and 80mg of caffeine in a low-sugar formulation. The range is available in 20-serve tubs with an RRP of £39.99. The launch further strengthens Myprotein’s position as a multi-category wellness brand, expanding its presence in the functional beverage market alongside its established sports nutrition portfolio. Brett Hamer, Product Director at Myprotein, said: “This is our first product to combine real coffee and protein. It taps into the on-the-go consumer mindset and addresses a clear market need for a product that delivers both the caffeine hit of an espresso shot and the protein of a dedicated supplement, all in a single, convenient format. “The Protein Iced Coffee range combines our expertise in performance nutrition with innovative product development, helping us deliver great taste alongside the functional benefits of protein. We know that consumers are looking for products that fit into daily life without compromising on nutrition, and that’s exactly what this range is designed to do.” The launch reflects broader consumer trends towards multifunctional products that offer convenience, taste and nutritional value, while creating further opportunities for Myprotein within the expanding ready-to-mix beverage category. The Protein Iced Coffee range is now available via Myprotein’s direct-to-consumer channels. Find more launches this summer. .. The five-year-young brand, best known for its mushroom coffees, hot chocolates and gummies, topped the poll after gaining 230% CAGR over the two most recent financial years. The Alantra Food & Beverage Fast 50 rankings showcases the best performing businesses in the sector with companies that have exceeded sales of £3m in the last year making the list. The 2026 index reveals Dirtea atop an all-functional top five. CBD drink brand Goodrays sits in silver spot, while Tonic, known for its effervescent vitamins and kids gummies, takes bronze. Another key CBD drinks player, Trip, stands in fourth place followed by the mushroom supplements brand Spacegoods. The theme runs throughout the poll with one third of all the businesses mentioned playing in the health and wellness space, including Bio&Me, Dr.Vegan, Bulk Powders, and Huel. “As a startup, we’ve always looked to Alantra as the biggest validation ever and what’s really cool is if you look at who has made the top three over the last five years, it’s all the brands that are now maturing or exiting,” said Dirtea co-founder Andrew Salter. “Trip have had an incredible story and are really cracking America now and gaining scale in retail, then you have Huel who just sold for a billion dollars, so to be named amongst those brands is really exciting.” Speaking about the factors that played into the brand’s fast growth, Salter he and his co-founding brother entered the market at the opportune time. Explore related questions Goodrays CBD drinks came in 2nd position (Goodrays) “When we started the brand most people would think I was nuts talking about drinking mushrooms but today it really has hit the mainstream.” The brand gained its first supermarket listing just this year with Tesco, and Salter admitted he’s been surprised by the organic sales. Tonic won third place (Tonic) “Our evolution from D2C, to running mushrooms bars in Selfridges, to gaining organic sales growth in a supermarket retailer like Tesco shows how much the market has evolved in the last five years,” he said. “Not only are Tesco shoppers interested in functional food and drink, but they already know and understand the Dirtea brand. I think when we start investing in marketing there, it’s going to be really impressive.” The Dirtea range recently expanded to include its first two non-mushrooms sku’s – pure creatine and pure collagen. Salter said these have been a huge success, with 86 per cent of the sales coming from those buying both products as a set, and 80 per cent of the sales on subscription. “It’s proves to us were are a trusted wellness platform, not just a mushroom brand,” he said. Fundamental socials Social media has also been an essential driver of growth. “Social media is fundamental for any brand wanting to grow but particularly for a brand that needs to educate the consumer. Something like mushrooms was niche and complex and we needed to educate through fun and memorable storytelling,” said Salter. “We put ourselves front and centre, as the founders, to tell our stories and educate the masses and our videos get up to six million views. Quality is what sets them apart. Table of Contents Shop from the Top 3 Mushroom Coffee Brands Different Mushroom Coffees for Different Buyers What Makes a Good Mushroom Coffee What to Avoid How We Ranked The 10 Best Mushroom Coffee Brands in the UK, Ranked What Mushroom Coffee Drinkers Say Mushroom Coffee Compared: Dose, Coffee and Price per Cup Final Thoughts Frequently Asked Questions Some of the links in this article are affiliate links, which help fund our independent review work at no extra cost to you. How we assessed these products is explained in this article and our Editor Lab methodology. No brand pays to appear, and no placement is guaranteed. Mushroom coffee has grown from a niche wellness drink into a crowded shelf, so the brand you pick matters more than ever. Balance Coffee comes out on top, with freshly roasted speciality coffee and the highest declared lion's mane dose here, 1,800mg a cup. DIRTEA is the best instant. You probably judge any mushroom coffee against your normal cup. Reviewers do the same, and their comments keep returning to steadier energy, fewer jitters, and less coffee. So the coffee half matters as much as the mushroom half. Most mushroom coffees put the mushroom first and build it on low-grade instant coffee. The best ones get both halves right. I compared 10 brands sold to UK buyers on real lion's mane dose, coffee base, coffee share, freshness, and price per cup, using the method in The Editor Lab . Editor's Note I am an SCA-certified barista with 14 years in the coffee trade. For this ranking I read every label, turned marketed equivalents back into real extract, and checked each coffee base and its freshness evidence in October 2026. Clemmie Rose, a registered nutritional therapist, reviewed the dose and safety content. Different Mushroom Coffees for Different Buyers Mushroom coffee splits into three types, and the right one depends on what you want from your cup. Start by deciding which type sounds like your morning. If you love coffee, you want fresh-roasted beans and a real dose, brewed the way you already brew. If you want a functional drink and do not mind losing the coffee ritual, an all-in-one blend suits you. If you want speed and a low price, instant is your type. By Category Visit the Job Board Search in https://dailycoffeenews.com/ Functional Instant Coffee Seller Reformed Gets $22 Million Round Daily Coffee News Staff | July 14, 2026 UK “functional coffee” and matcha company Reformed has raised a US$22 million Series A round led by Iris Ventures , with plans for a U.S. launch.  Launched by Neil Saada and Neil Marrakchi in 2024, Reformed sells powdered arabica coffee and “ceremonial-grade matcha” products blended with functional ingredients such as collagen, creatine, mushrooms, vitamins and minerals.  “In just two years, the company has scaled to over $70M in annualised revenue, achieved profitability, built a highly engaged community and become one of Europe’s fastest-growing consumer brands,” Iris Ventures said in a LinkedIn announcement . Marrakchi told Tech Funding New s that Reformed is targeting a $100 million revenue run rate by the end of 2026, with a U.S. launch planned for the third quarter. The company is part of a growing field of startups positioning coffee and coffee-adjacent products around concepts of wellness, supplements and daily rituals. In the U.S., Austin, Texas-based Everyday Dose has built a following around mushroom coffee blended with collagen and nootropics, while mushroom-coffee brand Ryze Superfoods has scaled around mushroom coffee through direct-to-consumer sales and social media. Forbes estimated earlier this year that Ryze could be worth $600 million in an acquisition.  U.S.-based Clevr Blends , a functional coffee and tea brand, has raised $2.78 million, according to PitchBook , while expanding beyond direct-to-consumer sales into Target stores.  In Europe, Reformed’s backer Iris Ventures has been building out a broader wellness and beauty portfolio, backing brands such as Healf, Goddess and Innerskin and Superlativa.  Comments? Questions? News to share? Contact DCN’s editors here . For all the latest coffee industry news, subscribe to the DCN newsletter . Moring and Webster met as mid teens in east London at a Romford ice rink. While Webster, who later ran his own building business, suffered from eczema and acne, Moring is also a lifelong coeliac. It wasn't long before the pair started researching the types of healthy food they should be eating, as well as keto and paleo lifestyles. Hunter & Gather started with 300 jars of mayonnaise stored in their living room. "We were in this underground world and we could see how bad the food system was becoming," recalls Moring. The childhood sweethearts say their first product occurred organically. "It didn't overly matter in our minds," says Moring. "It was about where we were going with the education piece, the lifestyle, content and marketing which was different to food brands of its time." Realising there were no seed oil free mayos on the market in Europe, they began contacting manufacturers and hit upon one looking at innovation — despite previously being told trial mayo runs wouldn't work without sugar. They sold their first batch within weeks, while a Whole Foods Market listing came within two months of launch. The pair kept their operation lean, with low overheads by working from their kitchen table and garden shed to prove the concept. It was, says Moring, a side hustle for three years as both kept their full-time jobs. "The earlier you go for equity, the more expensive it is in the long-term and difficult to get the equity back," admits Moring. The duo today own more than 50% of the company. _fonte: Heineken ventures into energy drinks, buys Tenzing holding - Global Drinks Intel Sign In News Beer Spirits Wine Environmental, Social & Governance Financial Results Marketing Mergers & Acquisitions New Product Development From the Industry Intel Comment Interview Category Intel Consumer Intel Market Intel Awards Global Drinks Awards New Product Awards ESG Awards Magazine Newsletter Subscribe Contact News Beer Spirits Wine Environmental, Social & Governance Financial Results Marketing Mergers & Acquisitions New Product Development From the Industry Intel Comment Interview Category Intel Consumer Intel Market Intel Awards Global Drinks Awards New Product Awards ESG Awards Magazine Newsletter Subscribe Contact Search Heineken ventures into energy drinks, buys Tenzing holding Last updated: 29/04/2025 at 4:13 PM By Intel Reporter 29 April 2025 2 Min Read ‘Tenzing is the only natural energy drink at scale – 100% plant-based, low in calories, and crafted with real fruit.’ SHARE The UK division of Heineken has purchased an unspecified size minority stake in the Tenzing “natural” energy drinks brand. The transaction, financial details of which were also not disclosed, has been secured on the basis of Tenzing retaining operational independence. Heineken UK will provide the brand with “limited distribution through its network into the convenience channel”. Huib Van Bockel, who founded the 100% plant-based brand in 2016 after spending nine years with Red Bull, will continue in his current role as CEO. “To take on the energy giants, we looked for a partner who could help us scale while staying true to who we are,” he said. “We had interest from several global players but chose Heineken because they share what matters most: a belief in craft, natural ingredients and building brands around community. They’re a family business that backs bold ideas and challenges the status quo. “We’ll learn from them – but it’s still that same team, running Tenzing independently.” Heineken UK MD Boudewijn Haarsma added: “Next to developing and stretching the beer and cider categories, which remain core to us, we are keen to selectively invest in growth markets beyond these. We’re proud to partner with a certified B-Corp company, one that has … a clear vision for the category and is totally committed to a product that is better for the consumer. “It is Heineken UK’s first investment into the rapidly growing energy drinks market, and we look forward to sharing valuable lessons and insights, as we help grow the Tenzing brand together.” In results from the first three months of this year, announced earlier this month , Heineken booked a flat sales performance thanks to a “high comparison base and … technical factors”. ‘We’re certainly not where we want to be yet – We’re more hungry’ – Heineken CEO Dolf van den Brink speaks to Global Drinks Intel TAGGED: Heineken Previous Article Waterloo Gin readies wider US assault with new pack look Next Article How start-up brands can use packaging to ‘engage in deeper conversations’ – Consumer Intel The Newsletter Sign up to receive our newsletter email The very latest news from across the world's beverage alcohol industry Cutting-edge intel from our in-depth category & market analyses, backed by benchmark industry data The best insight on your competitors from our interviews with the industry’s leaders Name This field is for validation purposes and should be left unchanged. Then look no further. I’ll take you through my favourite blends, including different varieties of instant and ground coffee. Despite how it may sound, mushroom coffee isn’t some crazy health fad that consists of brewing mushrooms in hot water. Nor is it a hallucinogenic drink. Nope, mushroom coffee is the new trendy way to drink coffee. It does indeed still include coffee as the main ingredient, but it has been mixed in with functional mushrooms like lion’s mane, reishi , chaga and cordyceps, to naturally enhance your day. You can also check out these amazing mushroom supplements . Many mushroom coffee products are popping up in the UK, so let me take you through my favourites. The coffee beans themselves are third-party tested for purity, meaning no mould or toxins. And it results in a cleaner coffee. As well as potentially avoiding any brain fog or gut issues. There is around 1,800mg of lion’s mane per cup and around 20% less caffeine, so you can enjoy steadier energy with less of the jitters! Plus, it tastes great too! They also make my favourite decaf – so be sure to check them out. Each cup of coffee contains 4000mg of lion’s mane mushroom from 100% fruiting bodies. The ground coffee is a single origin arabica blend from Ethiopia and has a lovely taste to it, which completely masks any mushroom taste. When you subscribe, one coffee costs just £0.76, also making this one of the more affordable mushroom coffees here! I don’t usually enjoy instant coffee, mostly due to the taste and mouthfeel, but London Nootropics have successfully made these into really drinkable coffee powders. Read my full London Nootropics review to find out more . The flavour is great and mixes really well with vegan milk to make an adaptogenic latte. The research expects that number to reach $478.1 million by 2033, with annual growth of 12.7% from 2026 onwards. The products people buy are also changing as Grand View Research found that capsules and tablets brought in the highest revenue in 2025. Drinks are expected to see the fastest growth over the next few years, because consumers want products that fit into daily routines… This trend appeared in The Nootropics Report 2.0, published a couple of years ago, which found rising interest in formats such as powders, gummies and ready to drink beverages designed for convenience and taste   What Do UK Buyers Want From Nootropics?   A lot of people hear the word nootropics and immediately think of prescription stimulants or Silicon Valley workers chasing endless productivity – that image feels outdated. Brainzyme’s guide says most UK buyers are shopping for legal products they can use every day without dealing with prescription rules or medical oversight. The guide says, “Most UK buyers are looking for safe, legal, daily brain support.” That is true. It also helps explain why natural supplements are doing well. Products containing ingredients such as L theanine, caffeine, choline, ginkgo biloba, B vitamins, rhodiola and the famous ashwagandha, are available over the counter in the UK. Brainzyme explains the category, saying, “Nootropics are substances associated with supporting cognitive function, mental clarity and focus.” Prescription products are in a separate category. Brainzyme says modafinil is a Schedule IV controlled substance in the UK and cannot legally be supplied without a prescription. Piracetam is also prescription only.   Which Ingredients Are Being Spoken About?   Consumer interest is not only about concentration because many buyers are shopping for products connected to things like sleep and overall mental wellbeing. In The Nootropics Report 2.0, dsm-firmenich said its 2023 Global Health Concerns Study found that 68% of consumers listed energy levels and tiredness as a top concern. 63% mentioned mental and emotional health, while 60% named mental performance Elena Gromoboeva, Global Dietary Supplements Lead for Brain Health at dsm-firmenich, said, “The brain health market is constantly growing and evolving, with more consumers looking for innovative ways to support total mind and body wellness.” This report also found caffeine continues to be the best known nootropic ingredient globally. And again, interest is also building around magnesium, B vitamins, ashwagandha, ginkgo, lion’s mane mushrooms and CBD in conversations around sleep and mood.   How Can Shoppers Choose Better Products?   The UK market is becoming more crowded, which makes label reading much more useful than having good looking branding. Brainzyme says shoppers should look for products that honestly and clearly list every ingredient and dosage. They look for products that avoid unrealistic claims and use research backed ingredient levels. Its guide says, “The single most useful quality signal is full per ingredient dose disclosure on the label.” A product calling itself a nootropic does not automatically say much about quality. Ingredient transparency and legal status usually count a lot more.   Which Startups Are Developing These Products?   These are 10 startups in the industry that are innovating:

One may use ground mushroom powder, another a concentrated extract, another may publish a beta-glucan percentage, and another may simply print a very large mushroom milligram number on the front of the pack. That makes headline dosage a poor way to compare the category on its own. For this guide we looked at beta-glucan standardisation, actual extract dose, extract specification, testing, caffeine, formulation, value and taste . We also personally tried every mushroom coffee in this comparison. Ancient Extracts makes Morning Magic, one of the products below, so this is not presented as an independent consumer-magazine review. We have made our criteria visible, shown where competitors genuinely outperform us, and separated published product specifications from our own taste judgement. Product details were checked on 28 August 2026. Our best overall pick Ancient Extracts Morning Magic Decaf Mushroom Coffee Three separate 15:1 mushroom extracts, each standardised to 30% beta-glucans, with every dose disclosed. That works out at approximately 252mg of beta-glucans per 6g serving from the published specification, alongside naturally decaffeinated Arabica and the best taste in our comparison. In simple terms, it gives you the Lion's Mane, Cordyceps and Chaga formula people are looking for from mushroom coffee without making the drink taste like mushrooms. Balance Coffee 6. Free Soul 7. Spacegoods Which tastes best? What to look for FAQs Final verdict The Shortlist Ancient Extracts Morning Magic: Best overall and best tasting DIRTEA Mushroom Coffee: Best published beta-glucan specification MOGU Mushroom Coffee: Best for a high disclosed multi-mushroom extract dose London Nootropics Flow: Best single-serve option Balance Lion's Mane Coffee: Best traditional ground coffee Free Soul Wake: Best broad lifestyle blend Spacegoods Rainbow Dust: Best for a high-dose adaptogen-style formula How We Compared the Mushroom Coffees Beta-glucan standardisation and extract transparency. This is one of the most important parts of our comparison. A product saying “1,000mg mushrooms” does not tell you whether that is raw powder, an extract, a concentrated extract or how much beta-glucan the ingredient is standardised to contain. We gave more credit when brands disclosed the mushroom species, extract dose and beta-glucan percentage rather than relying on one large marketing number. Actual amount per serving. Percentage is only half the story. A 45% extract at 250mg and a 30% extract at 840mg total are not the same thing. Where a brand clearly publishes both dose and beta-glucan percentage, we can calculate an approximate amount from those specifications. Taste. We tried every product in this guide because mushroom coffee still has to be something you actually want to drink. There is little point buying an impressive-looking functional formula if the earthy flavour makes it sit untouched in the cupboard. Alongside the flat whites and oat lattes, there are now mushroom lattes, protein coffees, and adaptogen-infused brews. And which products are worth your money if you want to try it at home? This beginner's guide covers everything you need to know about the UK functional coffee trend — no jargon, no hype, just honest advice from people who actually drink the stuff. What Is Functional Coffee? Functional coffee is regular coffee — Arabica beans, ground or instant — that's been blended with ingredients that offer additional health benefits beyond caffeine. Think of it as coffee that works harder. Mushroom Coffee — The Trend Leader Mushroom coffee is exactly what it sounds like: finely ground Arabica coffee blended with powdered medicinal mushrooms. Brew it in your cafetiere or pour-over for a morning cup that supports concentration. The Lion's Mane is front and centre here — 250g of properly good coffee with the cognitive benefits built in. 🥉 Best Low-Caffeine Option — Rheal Shroom Coffee Rheal's Shroom Coffee uses a low-caffeine Arabica base blended with Lion's Mane. 60 servings per tub, and it's organic and plant-based. Alongside the flat whites and oat lattes, there are now mushroom lattes, protein coffees, and adaptogen-infused brews. It's not a passing fad — functional coffee is reshaping how Brits think about their morning cup. But what actually is functional coffee? Does it taste like mushrooms? And which products are worth your money if you want to try it at home? This beginner's guide covers everything you need to know about the UK functional coffee trend — no jargon, no hype, just honest advice from people who actually drink the stuff. What Is Functional Coffee? Functional coffee is regular coffee — Arabica beans, ground or instant — that's been blended with ingredients that offer additional health benefits beyond caffeine. Think of it as coffee that works harder. The main categories dominating UK shelves in 2026 are: Mushroom coffee — ground Arabica blended with medicinal mushrooms like Lion's Mane, Chaga, Cordyceps, and Reishi Protein coffee — instant or brewed coffee with added whey or plant protein, popular in the fitness community Adaptogen blends — coffee with adaptogenic herbs like Ashwagandha, Maca Root, or Rhodiola for stress support Nootropic coffee — enhanced with ingredients like L-Theanine or collagen for focus and skin health The BBC reported in early 2026 that mushroom coffee on UK coffee shop menus has grown 30% in the past year alone. The trend is driven by the same wellness movement that brought us matcha, kombucha, and functional mushrooms — but with the advantage that it's still coffee , so you don't have to give up your morning ritual to try it. Mushroom Coffee — The Trend Leader Mushroom coffee is exactly what it sounds like: finely ground Arabica coffee blended with powdered medicinal mushrooms. Before you wrinkle your nose, the good news is it doesn't taste like a forest floor. Most blends use the fruiting body extract of mushrooms, which has an earthy, slightly nutty flavour that complements coffee surprisingly well. The most popular mushrooms you'll find in UK functional coffee are: Lion's Mane — the star ingredient, linked to focus, memory, and cognitive clarity Chaga — rich in antioxidants, known for immune support Cordyceps — traditionally used for energy and athletic performance Reishi — the calming mushroom, great for stress reduction Best Mushroom Coffees to Try 🏆 Best All-Round Starter — Mushroom Coffee Blend (Instant) This UK-made instant blend combines Lion's Mane, Cordyceps, Chaga, Reishi, and more with smooth Arabica coffee. 40 servings per pack, and it dissolves in hot water just like your regular instant. Brew it in your cafetiere or pour-over for a morning cup that supports concentration. The Lion's Mane is front and centre here — 250g of properly good coffee with the cognitive benefits built in. 🥉 Best Low-Caffeine Option — Rheal Shroom Coffee Rheal's Shroom Coffee uses a low-caffeine Arabica base blended with Lion's Mane. 60 servings per tub, and it's organic and plant-based. Ideal if you love the ritual of coffee but want to cut back on caffeine without going fully decaf. The concept is simple: take your regular coffee and add a source of protein — either as a pre-mixed instant powder or by adding a scoop of your favourite protein to brewed coffee. Alongside the flat whites and oat lattes, there are now mushroom lattes, protein coffees, and adaptogen-infused brews. It's not a passing fad — functional coffee is reshaping how Brits think about their morning cup. But what actually is functional coffee? Does it taste like mushrooms? And which products are worth your money if you want to try it at home? This beginner's guide covers everything you need to know about the UK functional coffee trend — no jargon, no hype, just honest advice from people who actually drink the stuff. What Is Functional Coffee? Functional coffee is regular coffee — Arabica beans, ground or instant — that's been blended with ingredients that offer additional health benefits beyond caffeine. Think of it as coffee that works harder. The main categories dominating UK shelves in 2026 are: Mushroom coffee — ground Arabica blended with medicinal mushrooms like Lion's Mane, Chaga, Cordyceps, and Reishi Protein coffee — instant or brewed coffee with added whey or plant protein, popular in the fitness community Adaptogen blends — coffee with adaptogenic herbs like Ashwagandha, Maca Root, or Rhodiola for stress support Nootropic coffee — enhanced with ingredients like L-Theanine or collagen for focus and skin health The BBC reported in early 2026 that mushroom coffee on UK coffee shop menus has grown 30% in the past year alone. The trend is driven by the same wellness movement that brought us matcha, kombucha, and functional mushrooms — but with the advantage that it's still coffee , so you don't have to give up your morning ritual to try it. Mushroom Coffee — The Trend Leader Mushroom coffee is exactly what it sounds like: finely ground Arabica coffee blended with powdered medicinal mushrooms. Before you wrinkle your nose, the good news is it doesn't taste like a forest floor. Most blends use the fruiting body extract of mushrooms, which has an earthy, slightly nutty flavour that complements coffee surprisingly well. Brew it in your cafetiere or pour-over for a morning cup that supports concentration. The Lion's Mane is front and centre here — 250g of properly good coffee with the cognitive benefits built in. 🥉 Best Low-Caffeine Option — Rheal Shroom Coffee Rheal's Shroom Coffee uses a low-caffeine Arabica base blended with Lion's Mane. 60 servings per tub, and it's organic and plant-based. Ideal if you love the ritual of coffee but want to cut back on caffeine without going fully decaf. The concept is simple: take your regular coffee and add a source of protein — either as a pre-mixed instant powder or by adding a scoop of your favourite protein to brewed coffee. _fonte: Holy Energy: Berliner Startup expandiert - Münster Aktuell Zum Inhalt springen Suche News Münster & Region Polizeimeldungen Freizeit Gastronomie Veranstaltungen Partys Veranstaltungskalender Interaktive Karte Münster Newsticker Münster Sport Münsterland persönlich Ratgeber News Münster & Region Polizeimeldungen Freizeit Gastronomie Veranstaltungen Partys Veranstaltungskalender Interaktive Karte Münster Newsticker Münster Sport Münsterland persönlich Ratgeber Holy Energy: Berliner Startup expandiert in Supermärkte Tim Eichler April 19, 2026 Symbolbild mit KI erstellt Teilen: Holy Energy ist der Name, der in der deutschen Getränkebranche gerade für Furore sorgt: Das Berliner Startup hat Energydrinks in Pulverform neu erfunden – und ist damit auf dem Weg, Red Bull und Monster Konkurrenz zu machen. Mit einem Umsatz von 170 Millionen Euro im Jahr 2025 und einer Investitionsrunde über 10,5 Millionen Euro zeigt Holy Energy, dass die Idee, Pulver statt Dose zu verkaufen, mehr als nur eine Nische ist. Anzeige Holy Energy: Wie das Berliner Startup den Getränkemarkt aufmischt Holy Energy wurde 2020 von Frederick Jost, Philipp Nass und Mathias Horsch in Berlin gegründet. Das Konzept ist denkbar einfach, aber revolutionär: Statt fertig abgefüllter Dosen verkauft Holy Energy aromatisiertes Pulver, das Kunden selbst mit Wasser mischen. Das spart Verpackungsmüll, reduziert Transportgewicht und macht den Konsum flexibler. Unter dem Markennamen Holy Energy gibt es klassische Energydrink-Varianten mit Koffein und Vitaminen, während Holy Hydration auf Elektrolyte für Sport und Alltag setzt. Beide Produktwelten kommen ohne Zuckerzusatz aus – ein Argument, das bei gesundheitsbewussten Konsumenten gut ankommt. Innerhalb weniger Jahre baute das Unternehmen eine loyale Community von 2,5 Millionen Kunden in sieben Märkten auf, darunter Deutschland, Frankreich, Polen und Großbritannien. Holy Energy Investition: 10,5 Millionen Euro und prominente Geldgeber Der Durchbruch als ernsthafter Marktplayer kam mit der Series-A-Finanzierungsrunde, in der Holy Energy 10,5 Millionen Euro einsammelte. Angeführt wurde die Runde vom globalen Wagniskapitalgeber Left Lane Capital. Damit stieg das gesamte eingeworbene Kapital des Berliner Startups auf rund 12,3 Millionen Euro. Zu den weiteren Investoren zählen FoodLabs, Simon Capital und der Londoner Konsumfonds V3 Ventures. Auch prominente Unternehmer beteiligten sich: Bela Seebach, Mitgründer von Just Spices, sowie Benjamin Kremer und Noel Bollmann, die Gründer von YFood, investierten in Holy Energy. Für die Startupszene in Deutschland gilt Holy Energy als Paradebeispiel dafür, wie innovative Geschäftsmodelle im Consumer-Goods-Bereich auch ohne klassisches Produktformat wachsen können. Das eingeworbene Kapital soll für die Sortimentserweiterung und die weitere Versorgung des stationären Handels genutzt werden. Holy Energy Supermarkt: 6.000 Geschäfte in Deutschland und Österreich Der nächste große Schritt für Holy Energy war die Offensive im stationären Einzelhandel. Im Januar 2026 startete das Unternehmen seine bislang größte Point-of-Sale-Kampagne: Auffällige Display-Auftritte in mehr als 6.000 Geschäften in Deutschland und Österreich, darunter Filialen von Rewe, Edeka und Globus, sorgten für ein bisher ungekanntes Markenbild im Regal. Zum ersten Mal war in jedem Starter-Set ein Rubbellos enthalten – mit der Chance, eines von zehn personalisierten Holy-Canyon-E-Bikes im Wert von je 3.000 Euro zu gewinnen. Für deutsche Startups , die den Sprung in den stationären Handel wagen, ist Holy Energy ein Vorzeigebeispiel: Vom reinen Online-Direktvertrieb zur flächendeckenden Supermarktpräsenz. Die Lebensmittelzeitung berichtete zudem, dass Holy Energy die Internationalisierung weiter beschleunigt und mittelfristig unter die Top-3-Energydrink-Marken in Europa vordringen will. Anzeige Holy Energy und Kritik: Was Verbraucherschützer warnen Nicht alle Stimmen zu Holy Energy sind positiv. Die Verbraucherzentrale Sachsen-Anhalt hat Warnungen zum Koffeingehalt des Pulvergetränks veröffentlicht und weist auf potenzielle Risiken hin, insbesondere für Kinder, Jugendliche und koffeinempfindliche Personen. Holy Energy enthält laut Produktangaben mikroverkapseltes Koffein, das nach Angaben des Unternehmens verträglicher sein soll als klassisches Koffein aus Energydosen. Ob das Produkt tatsächlich gesünder als herkömmliche Energydrinks ist, lässt sich pauschal nicht sagen und hängt von der individuellen Dosierung ab. Verbraucher sollten die Produktinformation aufmerksam lesen und die empfohlene Tagesdosis nicht überschreiten. Holy Energy gibt an, auf natürliche Zutaten zu setzen und volle Transparenz über die Inhaltsstoffe zu bieten. The event went down this past weekend, and the brand had a few new items to show fans, including a hybrid protein supplement. One of the innovations from Neosupps this month is Protein Iced Coffee, a hybrid coffee-flavored protein powder. The newly released Protein Iced Coffee from Neosupps is made of the exact ingredients you think it would, with whey concentrate for the protein and instant coffee for an authentic taste. The nutrition profile isn’t as lean as most competitors but within reason at 20g of protein, just shy of 5g of carbohydrates, between a gram and 2g of that sugar, 1.6 to 2.2g of fat, around 115 calories, and 80mg of caffeine from the coffee. Neosupps Protein Iced Coffee is a simple supplement, or as simple as combining two worlds can be, although the critical feature of this is the taste. The European brand has given its coffee protein hybrid two options: one is a traditional coffee experience in Hazelnut Macchiato, and the other is more like a protein powder in Cookies & Cream. Both are available straight from the brand’s website at a low €22.99, but that is for a smaller than usual 500g tub of about 16 servings. The all-new Protein Iced Coffee comes in Chai Latte, Vanilla Caramel Latte, a rich Chocolate, sweet White Chocolate, and Hazelnut Macchiato. The innovation is basically a lean whey protein powder with a genuine coffee taste, and that does infuse a bit of caffeine at 80mg per serving. The price on the product is not too bad sitting at €29.99 (35.31 USD), and that’ll get you a standard 2lb tub for about 30 servings. Getränketrends Low- & No-ABV Themen-Plan 2026 PR-Service Mediadaten Jobbörse Suche Menü Menü koawach Ready-to-go-Drink erobert Lebensmitteleinzelhandel 08.05.2017 / in AFG , Getränke , News / von Redaktion teilen   teilen   teilen   Nach dem erfolgreichen Start des Wachmacher-Kakaos in Pulverform erobert koawach den deutschen Einzelhandel jetzt aufs Neue. Milchprodukte rücken im Kühlregal näher zusammen und machen Platz für den neuen koawach Drink in den Geschmacksrichtungen „Klassik“ und „Pfefferminz“. Im To-go-Drink vereinen sich fair gehandelte Bio-Zutaten aus Lateinamerika – Kakao, belebendes Guarana und Rohrzucker – mit frischer Bio-Kuhmilch aus den deutschen und österreichischen Bergen. Erhältlich ist der wachmachende Schoko-Drink bereits in etwa 7.200 deutschen Märkten. Schon bei der Produkteinführung war koawach bundesweit in allen Märkten von real vorrätig. Nicht mal zwei Monate später verzeichnet koawach weitere volle Listungen bei Edeka Nord, Kaufland, REWE und PENNY. Hinzukommen stetige Produktaktionen mit unterschiedlichen Händlern wie zum Beispiel Netto und Lidl. koawach liefert mit den vielfältigen Pulvern und den To-go-Drinks „Klassik“ und „Pfefferminz“ den nachhaltigen Energiekick. Deshalb legt koawach auch bei seinen Verpackungen großen Wert auf Nachhaltigkeit und verpackt die schokoladigen Drinks in die 235 ml „Cartocans“, die nicht nur aus umweltfreundlichem Karton bestehen, sondern auch recycelbar sind. Über koawach: koawach und die koakult GmbH wurden im Jahr 2014 von Heiko Butz und Daniel Duarte gegründet. Die beiden Gründer haben sich bei Studenteninitiativen zum Thema Nachhaltigkeit kennen- und als Geschäftspartner schätzen gelernt. Nachdem sie sich im Oktober 2015 bei der VOX-Sendung „Die Höhle der Löwen“ der härtesten Gründer-Jury Deutschlands gestellt hatten, entwickelte sich die koakult GmbH mit großen Schritten weiter. Die verschiedenen koawach Produkte verbinden den schokoladigen Genuss aus Lateinamerika mit dem brasilianischen Wachmacher Guarana. koawach verzichtet auf sämtliche künstliche Zusatzstoffe und verarbeitet lediglich hochwertige sowie fair gehandelte Rohstoffe aus ökologischem Anbau. News von Marc Nemitz · München, 30. Juli 2025 Gründerbild ciao coffee Das Münchener Startup ciao coffee hat eine Pre-Seed-Finanzierungsrunde im mittleren sechsstelligen Bereich abgeschlossen. Angeführt wird die Runde vom Impact-Investorennetzwerk better ventures , beteiligt sind zudem mehrere Business Angels aus den Bereichen FMCG, E-Commerce und FoodTech. Ziel der Finanzierung ist es, die Kaffee-Alternative der nächsten Generation im Markt zu etablieren und weiterzuentwickeln. Impact-Investoren setzen auf nachhaltige Kaffee-Alternative Mit dem frischen Kapital will ciao coffee gezielt in Markenaufbau, Retail-Expansion und Produktentwicklung investieren. better ventures sieht in ciao coffee großes Potenzial für einen nachhaltigen Wandel im Getränkemarkt. Auch Investoren aus der Konsumgüter- und Medienbranche, wie Christoph Behn, Kathrin Pucknat und Thomas Gros, beteiligen sich an der Runde. ciao coffee zeigt, wie neue Marken mutig Märkte neu denken – mit einem klaren Blick auf Nachhaltigkeit, Funktionalität, Gesundheit und Genuss Tina Dreimann, Mitgründerin und Geschäftsführerin von better ventures Gegründet wurde das Start-up 2024 von Tobias Hollaus, Felix Hellenberg, Dennis von Bismarck und Anton Reich. Das Team verfügt über langjährige Erfahrung aus FMCG, Food Innovation und Markenführung (u. a. yfood , foodspring , Mondelez und Jacobs). Kaffee ohne Bohne neu gedacht Das Produktkonzept von ciao coffee basiert auf einer Rezeptur ganz ohne Kaffeebohnen. Stattdessen kommen europäische Zutaten wie Roggen, Gerste, Zichorie und Löwenzahnwurzel zum Einsatz. Die Mischung enthält zudem gezielt zugesetztes Koffein, einen Vitamin-B-Komplex und Eisen, der für eine langanhaltende Wachheit ohne klassischen Koffeincrash sorgen soll. Zwar setzt ciao coffee auf bekannte Zutaten wie Zichorie, Gerste und Roggen, die unter Namen wie Landkaffee oder Muckefuck schon lange als koffeinfreie und bekömmliche Kaffeealternativen bekannt sind. Die Idee, diese traditionellen Produkte durch gezielte Anreicherung mit Koffein, Vitaminen und Eisen funktional aufzuwerten, ist zwar innovativ gedacht, doch nicht unumstritten. Kritiker könnten sich fragen, ob die Kombination aus bewusstem Verzicht und stimulierenden Zusatzstoffen nicht einem Widerspruch gleichkommt. Während sich einige Konsumenten vom funktionalen Mehrwert angesprochen fühlen dürften. Es bleibt abzuwarten, ob der Markt diese Neuinterpretation auch langfristig als eigenständige Kategorie akzeptiert. Erfolgreicher Markteintritt in DACH Trotz der frühen Phase zeigt ciao coffee bereits starke Traktion im Lebensmitteleinzelhandel. Das Produkt ist derzeit in über 500 Filialen von REWE, EDEKA und Billa Plus in Deutschland und Österreich gelistet. Die Verkaufszahlen bewegen sich laut Unternehmen auf Augenhöhe mit etablierten Ready-to-Drink-Marken wie Starbucks oder Emmi. Auch das neue Packaging, das aktuell deutschlandweit ausgerollt wird, sorgt laut Handelspartnern für positive Resonanz und steigende Abverkäufe. Weitere Gespräche mit zusätzlichen Retailpartnern laufen, mit dem Ziel, das Vertriebsnetz um rund 1.000 weitere Verkaufsstellen auszubauen. Fokus auf nachhaltige und funktionale Getränkekonzepte ciao coffee trifft einen doppelten Zeitgeist: gesundheitsbewusster Koffeinkonsum und ökologisch verantwortungsvolle Ernährung. Der Markt für funktionale Getränke in Europa wird auf mehrere Milliarden Euro geschätzt. ciao coffee adressiert zudem die wachsende Zielgruppe von Menschen mit Unverträglichkeiten gegenüber klassischem Kaffee. Search All articles What is the purpose of each ingredient of Clearly Not Coffee? Updated 9 months ago – Cacao Cacao is the rich, chocolatey base of Clearly Not Coffee. It's naturally packed with antioxidants, magnesium, and gentle plant-based stimulants like theobromine. These compounds can boost your mood, support focus, and provide a smoother, more stable energy lift compared to traditional caffeine. Plus, cacao gives Clearly Not Coffee its deep, comforting flavor. – Maca Maca is an adaptogenic root from the Andes, traditionally used to balance energy levels, support endurance, and promote hormonal balance. In Clearly Not Coffee, it adds a subtle malt-like flavor while helping you feel energized and resilient throughout the day. – Lion’s Mane Lion’s Mane is a superstar mushroom known for its brain-boosting benefits. It supports cognitive function, memory, and mental clarity by stimulating the production of Nerve Growth Factor (NGF), which plays a role in brain health. It's a key reason why Clearly Not Coffee is often used for clean, focused energy. – Reishi Reishi, often called the "Mushroom of Immortality," brings a sense of calm and balance. It helps manage stress, support immunity, and encourage overall wellness. In Clearly Not Coffee, it rounds out the energy boost with a soothing adaptogenic effect. – Chaga Chaga is another powerful mushroom known for its incredibly high antioxidant content. It supports immune health, reduces oxidative stress, and helps keep your body resilient. Chaga's subtle earthiness adds depth to the flavor profile. – Cordyceps Cordyceps are famous for promoting natural energy production and endurance. They help improve oxygen utilization and stamina, making them a perfect addition to a blend designed for sustained, clean energy without the crash. – Maitake Maitake mushrooms support a healthy immune response and may help with blood sugar balance. Including Maitake helps make Clearly Not Coffee a more complete adaptogenic and immune-supportive blend. – Cinnamon Cinnamon adds a warm, sweet-spicy flavor while also delivering health benefits like supporting blood sugar stability, fighting inflammation, and acting as a natural antioxidant. It complements the cacao beautifully and rounds out the taste. – Himalayan Salt A small touch of Himalayan salt helps replenish essential minerals and support hydration. It also enhances the overall flavor of the mix, bringing out the richness of the cacao and the warmth of the spices. – Rhodiola Rhodiola is an adaptogen famous for reducing fatigue and supporting mental performance. It helps the body adapt to physical and emotional stress, making it a key part of the blend’s smooth, non-jittery energy. – Reb M Reb M is a clean, naturally derived sweetener from the stevia leaf. It provides a subtle hint of sweetness without the bitterness often associated with stevia. This allows Clearly Not Coffee to taste amazing without any added sugar or artificial sweeteners. Last updated: March 6, 2024 by Michael Joseph, MSc, ANutr There has been quite a buzz over the purported benefits of mushroom coffee, with one product, in particular, gaining significant popularity. This product goes by the name of RYZE mushroom coffee, and it claims to provide better focus, energy, gut health, and bolster the immune system. But does the addition of dried mushrooms to coffee truly have such benefits? This article delves into RYZE mushroom coffee and assesses whether it lives up to the touted benefits in its marketing claims. What Is RYZE Mushroom Coffee? Before we investigate the claims of health benefits, let’s first explore exactly what RYZE mushroom coffee comprises. Ingredients According to the product’s ingredients label, it contains eight ingredients. These are as follows ( 1 ): Cordyceps Lion’s Mane Reishi Shiitake Turkey tail King Trumpet MCT oil Coffee The first six of these ingredients are all various types of mushrooms. Some of these mushrooms are commonly available on store shelves, such as shiitake, while others can be more difficult to find. Regarding MCT oil, the MCT abbreviation stands for ‘medium-chain triglycerides’. Triglycerides are a type of fat, so in other words, it is an oil made up of medium-chain fatty acids ( 2 ). Medium-chain fatty acids are a kind of saturated fat that only have between six and twelve carbon atoms in their chain (structure). They are easier for the body to metabolize compared to fatty acids with longer chains ( 2 ). As they lack a strong flavor, MCT oils can be used in products without overly influencing the overall taste. The MCT oil in RYZE mushroom coffee has been produced from coconuts ( 1 ). Dose Per Serving RYZE mushroom coffee provides no information on the amount of each mushroom that the product contains per serving. However, the company do state that a serving of the product (1 scoop) weighs six grams. Furthermore, each serving contains a total of two grams of ‘organic mushroom blend’ ( 1 ). Although there are no precise, exact conversions, mushrooms are generally 80-90% water. Thus, two grams of dried mushrooms would be equivalent to a maximum of around 20 grams of fresh, hydrated mushrooms ( 3 , 4 ). From the ‘two grams’ blend of dried mushrooms, we can assume that there may be around 0.33 grams of each of the six dried mushrooms per serving. The final four grams (per serving) of the product is a mixture of MCT oil and coffee. Nutritional Properties According to the RYZE mushroom coffee website, each serving of the product has the following nutritional profile ( 1 ): Calories: 15 kcal Carbohydrates: 0.58 g Fiber: 0.48 g Fat: 1.42 g Protein: 0.05 g Cholesterol: 0 mg Sodium: 0 mg Does It Contain Caffeine? All products containing coffee will naturally provide a source of caffeine, and RYZE mushroom coffee is no different. However, since more than 60% of the ‘serving’ is dried mushrooms, it contains less coffee than most pure coffee products. According to the company, a cup of RYZE mushroom coffee has a caffeine content of 48 mg ( 1 ). This is approximately half the amount of caffeine you’d typically find in a cup of coffee. How Does It Taste? Mushroom coffee tastes slightly like instant coffee , but with a subtle difference. This distinction can be attributed to the extra flavor notes the mushrooms offer, with an “earthy” taste being a common descriptor that I’d agree with. It doesn’t quite have the same bold coffee flavor as a cup of pure coffee would, but it does taste similar. It is likely that anyone who enjoys coffee would also like this product. Key Point: RYZE mushroom coffee is a drink blend featuring two grams of dried mushrooms and a combined four grams of powdered coffee and MCT oil. Is RYZE Mushroom Good For You? Now that we’ve established what RYZE mushroom coffee is, let’s explore some of its potential benefits and downsides. Benefits Here are some of the benefits (and potential benefits) of the product. Lower Caffeine Content Than Regular Coffee With only 48 mg of caffeine per cup serving, RYZE mushroom coffee boasts a lower caffeine content compared to typical coffee drinks. While the caffeine content of coffee can vary tremendously, assessments of the caffeine content of various drinks indicate that ( 5 , 6 , 7 ): Brewed coffee typically contains 58-259 mg of caffeine per serving Instant coffee typically contains around 60 mg of caffeine per drink From these data, we can infer that RYZE mushroom coffee provides less caffeine than other coffee beverages. Some brewed coffee drinks may contain as much as four times its caffeine content, depending on the specific coffee. It is important to note that caffeine can have a range of benefits and downsides. Having found fame with its pioneering fat and coffee blend over the last decade, the company now sees interest in functional coffees going mainstream: and it’s repositioning to tap into that opportunity. Its products and ingredients (based on the brand’s signature butter-coffee blend but also include additional add-ons such as gut health, collagen, mental focus and more) remain unchanged: but new language and branding will make its functional positioning clear to a wider audience. Butter coffee beginnings Founded in 2011, Bulletproof found fame with its coffee and fat blend: a high-calorie caffeinated drink that replaces carb-heavy breakfasts. The coffee’s star ingredients are high-quality coffee, MCT oil and grass-fed ghee (or butter), that promotes sustained energy, increased satiety and cognitive function support. The brand was created by Dave Asprey: a successful Silicon Valley entrepreneur who was inspired by a creamy cup of yak butter tea while trekking in Tibet. That idea was then turned into Bulletproof coffee: ‘ a high-performance drink that has a massive impact on your energy and cognitive function ’. Bulletproof Coffee The Bulletproof Diet was created by American entrepreneur and author Dave Asprey, spearheaded by his Bulletproof Coffee brand. Bulletproof’s Brain Octane C8 MCT Oil, derived from 100% coconuts (no palm oil), rapidly converts into ketones: offering fast, sustained energy that supports brain and body without the blood sugar spike. Bulletproof Coffee found a cult following with keto enthusiasts, intermittent fasters and performance minded biohackers: and the term ‘bulletproof’ is now know beyond the brand. “Bulletproof’s USP centers on delivering clean, functional products that deliver sustained energy, mental clarity, and metabolic support—without the crash,” explained Andy van Ark, CCO of Bulletproof. “We have built a portfolio around the coffee experience to meet the needs of health focused consumers, including supporting brain power, metabolic function, and energy, making it ideal for people who want more out of their morning coffee experience.” And those people who want more out of their coffee experience are growing in number. So is their knowledge of functional ingredients. Back in 2011, ingredients such as MCT oil and collagen were niche. Today, functionality has a far wider demand, said van Ark: and the brand is repositioning itself to be accommodate a much wider audience. “This evolution was a natural next step,” he continued. “While Bulletproof started in the biohacking world, the need for clean energy, focus, and wellness support has become universal. We saw an opportunity to make functional coffee more approachable for a broader audience—without losing what made us different. Our mission is to help people, whether they identify as a biohacker or not, to feel better, think clearer, and start their day stronger.” Bulletproof’s portfolio has already evolved alongside mainstream consumer trends: from ground coffee to coffee pods and coldbrew. Stacker-Food & Drink Americans wanted a coffee alternative. The one they picked still has coffee in it. By Stacker Published October 27, 2026 11:49 AM By Scott Needham for SmartScout New SmartScout data shows RYZE, a mushroom coffee blend, now brings in more revenue than Nescafé or Starbucks in Amazon’s Instant Coffee category. The caffeine alternatives made without coffee are growing at a fraction of that pace, and several of the best-known names are shrinking.   RYZE blends mushroom powders with a smaller dose of coffee and sells it as a gentler way to start the day. On Amazon, it is now the top brand in Instant Coffee, with 18.7% of category revenue, or $3,374,391 a month. Nescafé is second at 13.2% and $2,376,174. Starbucks is third at 11.4% and $2,052,561. Taster’s Choice, Mount Hagen and Folgers follow, each with less than 6%. RYZE gets there with far fewer units. It moves 68,025 units per month in the category, against 192,592 for Nescafé. Its average listing price is $67.21, roughly double Nescafé’s $32.50 and Starbucks’ $38.20. It needs nine listings to do it. Nescafé has 159. Across all 22 of its products, RYZE brings in $4,191,101 a month, or $75,938,416 a year. That is up 43.2% from a year ago, and every sale goes through a single seller. A product marketed as a way off coffee is now the best-selling coffee in its aisle. SmartScout Fewer Searches, More Sales The growth is happening while interest, measured by search, is falling. Searches for “ryze mushroom coffee” fell 21.3% over the past year, from 439,680 a month to 346,056. Searches for the generic term “mushroom coffee” fell 22.2%, to 195,516. The rest of the category followed. Searches for Cuppa mushroom coffee fell 22.9%. Four Sigmatic fell 19.1%. Everyday Dose fell 76.4%, to 12,880 a month. Laird was the one brand search that grew, up 20.1%. Revenue moved the other way. RYZE is up 43.2%. Everyday Dose, despite the collapse in searches for its name, grew revenue 12%, to $20,463,289 a year. One reading of the gap is that mushroom coffee has stopped being new. Shoppers who already drink it do not search for it. They reorder. The curiosity phase is ending. The habit phase pays better. Coffee Itself Is Still Growing The idea that Americans are quitting coffee does not show up in Amazon&#8217

Stacker-Food & Drink Americans wanted a coffee alternative. The one they picked still has coffee in it. By Stacker Published October 27, 2026 11:49 AM By Scott Needham for SmartScout New SmartScout data shows RYZE, a mushroom coffee blend, now brings in more revenue than Nescafé or Starbucks in Amazon’s Instant Coffee category. The caffeine alternatives made without coffee are growing at a fraction of that pace, and several of the best-known names are shrinking.   RYZE blends mushroom powders with a smaller dose of coffee and sells it as a gentler way to start the day. On Amazon, it is now the top brand in Instant Coffee, with 18.7% of category revenue, or $3,374,391 a month. Nescafé is second at 13.2% and $2,376,174. Starbucks is third at 11.4% and $2,052,561. Taster’s Choice, Mount Hagen and Folgers follow, each with less than 6%. RYZE gets there with far fewer units. It moves 68,025 units per month in the category, against 192,592 for Nescafé. Its average listing price is $67.21, roughly double Nescafé’s $32.50 and Starbucks’ $38.20. It needs nine listings to do it. Nescafé has 159. Across all 22 of its products, RYZE brings in $4,191,101 a month, or $75,938,416 a year. That is up 43.2% from a year ago, and every sale goes through a single seller. A product marketed as a way off coffee is now the best-selling coffee in its aisle. SmartScout Fewer Searches, More Sales The growth is happening while interest, measured by search, is falling. Searches for “ryze mushroom coffee” fell 21.3% over the past year, from 439,680 a month to 346,056. Searches for the generic term “mushroom coffee” fell 22.2%, to 195,516. The rest of the category followed. Searches for Cuppa mushroom coffee fell 22.9%. Four Sigmatic fell 19.1%. Everyday Dose fell 76.4%, to 12,880 a month. Laird was the one brand search that grew, up 20.1%. Revenue moved the other way. RYZE is up 43.2%. Everyday Dose, despite the collapse in searches for its name, grew revenue 12%, to $20,463,289 a year. One reading of the gap is that mushroom coffee has stopped being new. Shoppers who already drink it do not search for it. They reorder. The curiosity phase is ending. The habit phase pays better. Analisi di un trend tra Instagram, benessere e neuroscienze fai-da-te Negli ultimi anni, tra le bevande che hanno guadagnato popolarità nel panorama del benessere, il mushroom coffee si è ritagliato un posto sempre più visibile di Ilaria Corona 30 Giugno, 2025 Salva Salva post Annulla Creare Creare collezione {{ item.title }} Carica altri Per vedere più contenuti su Google, aggiungici alle fonti preferite Aggiungi Gambero Rosso Per vedere più contenuti, aggiungici alle fonti preferite Aggiungi Gambero Rosso di Ilaria Corona 30/06/25 Amato da chi cerca un’alternativa più gentile al caffè tradizionale e promosso come tonico naturale per mente e corpo, il caffè ai funghi unisce la cultura del caffè di qualità agli estratti di funghi medicinali, alcuni usati da secoli nella medicina tradizionale cinese. Ma che cos’è davvero questa bevanda diventata ormai un cult del benessere? Cos’è il caffè ai funghi? Il caffè ai funghi è una miscela di caffè vero e proprio, normalmente arabica, con l’aggiunta di polveri o estratti derivati dai cosiddetti funghi funzionali. Tra i più utilizzati si trovano il lion’s mane (Hericium erinaceus), il reishi (Ganoderma lucidum), il chaga (Inonotus obliquus), i cordyceps e il turkey tail (Trametes versicolor). Ciascuno di questi funghi è tradizionalmente associato a determinati effetti benefici: miglioramento della memoria e della concentrazione, rafforzamento del sistema immunitario, maggiore resistenza fisica o riduzione dello stress. A differenza dei funghi psichedelici, i funghi funzionali non hanno alcun effetto allucinogeno o psicoattivo. La preparazione è piuttosto semplice. Le aziende produttrici solitamente tostano caffè di qualità e vi aggiungono polveri derivate da estratti fungini, spesso realizzati tramite un processo a doppia estrazione che dovrebbe garantire una maggiore disponibilità dei composti attivi. Il risultato è una bevanda calda, simile al caffè normale per aspetto e sapore, ma con una dose di caffeina più bassa. In media, una tazza di mushroom coffee contiene tra i 40 e i 60 milligrammi di caffeina , contro i circa 95 milligrammi del caffè tradizionale. Esistono anche versioni completamente prive di caffeina, pensate per chi desidera limitare o eliminare del tutto questo stimolante. Il fascino crescente di questa bevanda La popolarità di questo caffè è legata alla promessa di una stimolazione più pulita e duratura, priva degli effetti collaterali talvolta associati al caffè, come l’ansia, il nervosismo. Alcuni consumatori riferiscono di sentirsi più lucidi e meno agitati, anche dopo il consumo quotidiano. A questo si aggiunge l’interesse, sempre più diffuso, per ingredienti naturali e funzionali, che vanno oltre la semplice nutrizione e ambiscono a supportare il benessere in modo olistico. Dal punto di vista scientifico, però, le evidenze sui benefici del mushroom coffee sono ancora limitate. La maggior parte degli studi che riguardano i funghi funzionali sono stati condotti su animali o in vitro, oppure si basano sull’impiego di alte dosi di estratti concentrati, ben superiori a quelle presenti in una normale tazza di caffè ai funghi. Per quanto riguarda il gusto, molti consumatori rimangono sorpresi nel constatare quanto poco sapore di fungo abbia effettivamente la bevanda. Le versioni ben formulate tendono a mascherare l’umidità e l’amarezza tipica dei funghi, mantenendo un profilo aromatico simile a quello del caffè tradizionale, talvolta con note leggermente terrose. In alcuni casi, la consistenza può risultare più corposa, ma nel complesso l’esperienza non si discosta molto da quella di una tazza di caffè convenzionale. Conquista anche le star A rafforzare la popolarità del mushroom coffee è senza dubbio il crescente interesse del mondo della moda e delle celebrità per questa bevanda, ormai protagonista anche su Instagram e nei menù dei caffè più trendy. Tra le più entusiaste sostenitrici figura Meghan Markle : la duchessa del Sussex, da tempo appassionata di benessere e alimentazione naturale, nel 2024 è apparsa in un video del marchio californiano Clevr Blends , che propone superfood latte arricchiti con funghi medicinali adattogeni e probiotici. Meghan non è solo fan del brand, ma anche investitrice, e con il suo endorsement ha contribuito a rendere virale questo caffè Il mushroom coffee segue così l’onda di altri trend funzionali amati dalle celebrity. Enter: coffee. And with the nutrition-packed Caffè Latte from the recently launched Strong Coffee Company, it's easier than ever to chase down your health goals without losing energy. Adam Von Rothfelder, Strong Coffee Company's founder & CEO, is a former MMA fighter who's trained NFL star Ray Lewis and been on NBC's fitness competition show Strong . Clearly, a good source of energy does wonders for him. But it wasn't a selfish need for nutritionally sound coffee that drove him to create the product. When Von Rothfelder's father was suffering from leukemia and resisting healthful foods, he decided to sneak nutrition into coffee, something he knew his dad wouldn't push away. View this post on Instagram Besides time-released caffeine to keep you going strong for hours, the keto-friendly Caffè Latte has collagen for muscle fuel, coconut water for hydration and MCTs to help boost your brain. Plus, it tastes good: There's a hint of sweetness that, when combined with the silky texture, might just trick you into thinking you're drinking a coffee milkshake. Whether you opt for the individual packets or a large, resealable bag, it couldn't be easier to prepare. You just mix it with hot or cold water, and eight seconds later you have a coffee drink that kills about five birds with one stone. Even if you're not trying on a keto diet for size, consider it a better investment than your daily coffee shop stop—bother in terms of time and money saved (you'll even get 15% off your first purchase with this link ). From a flurry of keto snacks and functional-but-fun beverages, to firms making more proactive claims about their impact (or lack thereof) on the environment, check out our first trendspotting gallery from the Natural Products Expo West show in Anaheim, CA. EXPO WEST 2022 trendspotting: From mushroom elixirs to climate-friendly crackers Fungi-fueled startup Odyssey taps into growing interest in mushroom extracts Launched last year and now in around 700 stores, Odyssey organic mushroom elixirs and brews feature meaningful amounts of Lion's Mane, Cordyceps, Reishi, Chaga, and Turkey Tail extracted from mushroom fruiting bodies, combined with tea, coffee, or sparkling water, says founder Scott Frohman, who said sales have " exploded," buoyed by growing interest in adaptogens and immunity. The beverages are billed as promoting energy, endurance, sleep, focus, immunity and mood. Feel good, do good: Maca-fueled Machu Picchu enters energy category Founded by Brazilian drinks industry veteran Bernardo Paiva and run by Startup CPG founder Daniel Scharrf, Machu Picchu Organic Energy (strapline: ' Feel good. Do good '*) is fueled by maca root extract, B vitamins, and 120mg caffeine from green coffee beans (Machu Picchu energy seltzers contain 40mg caffeine). The brand (SRP $2.99) - which has secured listings at Erewhon, Central Market (H-E-B), and Gopuff, with UNFI and KeHE now on board to distribute - checks all the right boxes for label readers (organic, no preservatives, no artificial flavors, colors, sweeteners etc), but has been a hit with buyers and consumers because it delivers on taste, claimed Scharrf. "Even if you don’t care that it’s organic and natural and doesn’t have preservatives, it just tastes better than anything else that's out there ." * Machu Picchu Energy partners with several organizations dedicated to improving the lives of children in the US and overseas. It is also is a founding member and backer of the 2030 Cultural Pact, a partnership with UNESCO in Peru to preserve cultural sites, including Machu Picchu. Culture Pop: Fun + functionality A new category is emerging in the soda aisle promising fun and functionality, says Nantucket Nectars founder and beverage industry veteran Tom First, who is combining familiar flavors (berries, ginger lemon, watermelon) with a culinary twist (basil, rosemary, chili, juniper) and the probiotic strain Bacillus Subtilis DE111 to create Culture Pop . The brand, which is available in seven regions of Whole Foods, is made with 23-24% organic juice, herbs and spices, with 40 calories and 6g sugar from fruit juice per can, says First, who is speaking at FoodNavigator-USA's ' Feeding the Gut Microbiome ' webinar on Thursday morning. Bored of Frappuccinos? Joy Milk Tea has the answer Chicago-based Joy Milk Tea - which combines milk, brewed black tea (delivering 130mg caffeine in a 11.5oz can), cane sugar and gum acacia in a shelf-stable format - is generating strong repeat rates, says founder Max Blessen, who says fans “ love to drink it as a morning pick me up or instead of coffee as an afternoon pick me up. “We’re merchandised next to RTD coffees and other premium beverages and we have great velocities of 12 to 18 units per week and some up to 60 units per store per week.” CBD beverage brands... we're in it for the long haul While the lack of clarity at a federal level over the regulatory status of ingestible CBD has thwarted growth, several CBD-infused beverage brands exhibited at Expo West, from UK-based TRIP to Sati CBD Soda , and insist that consumer interest remains strong. Q3 2026 earnings summary 10 Sep, 2026 Executive summary Achieved record quarterly net revenue of $11.5 million (CAD 11.5 million), up 10.3% year-over-year and 27% on a comparable basis, marking the highest to date. U.S. net revenue surged 59.8% to $2.8 million, driven by expanded natural-channel distribution and new nationwide listings. Canadian net revenue was stable year-over-year but grew 19% on a comparable basis, supported by new product launches and expanded shelf space. Net income reached $0.5 million with positive Adjusted EBITDA of $0.9 million, marking the third consecutive trailing-twelve-month period of positive Adjusted EBITDA. Leadership transition announced: CEO stepping down after 12 years, Board searching for successor, with interim co-leadership by CFO and COO. Financial highlights Net revenue for Q3 2026 was $11.5 million, up from $10.4 million in Q3 2025; nine-month net revenue rose 17.3% to $28.9 million. Gross margin was 61.9%, down from 71.3% last year (or 65.9% comparable), mainly due to increased trade and promotional spend. SG&A expenses were $6.7 million in Q3 2026, improving as a percentage of revenue to 58.5% from 60.6%. Net income for Q3 2026 was $0.5 million; nine-month net loss improved to $0.8 million. Liquidity remains strong with $25.6 million in cash, $10 million undrawn facility, and no debt. Outlook and guidance Entering the final quarter with strong momentum, focusing on scaling Zero Sugar products and expanding U.S. distribution in targeted channels. Margin expected to trend back toward structural levels through disciplined pricing, trade, and continued investment in growth channels. Functional mushrooms are specific types of fungi celebrated for health-boosting properties that go far beyond basic nutrition. Unlike regular culinary mushrooms, varieties like Lion’s Mane, Reishi, and Cordyceps are packed with active compounds and adaptogens —natural substances that help your body manage and resist stress. BevNET Press Releases Collective Arts Carves Out a New Space in Clean, Functional Energy with Botany PRESS RELEASE posted by Collective Arts Dec. 15, 2025 at 10:42 am X LinkedIn Reddit Facebook Email Report Press Release energy functional energy clean energy drinks wellness lifestyle women balance adaptogens Non-Alcoholic Beverages Botany Energy: Inspired by women looking for more modern, balanced ways to stay energized Hamilton, ON — December 12, 2025 — Collective Arts, the Canadian craft beverage company known for pushing the boundaries of creativity and innovation, today announced the launch of Botany Energy, a new line of clean energy drinks. The introduction of Botany Energy marks Collective Arts' continued expansion beyond craft beer and into the fast-growing functional beverage market. Botany brings a fresh perspective to the energy drink category, blending thoughtful formulation with signature eye-catching design. Each product is crafted to fit the way people want to feel today: focused but not wired, energized but still grounded, supported throughout the day without the extremes. Energy is no longer a one-size-fits-all category. Consumers are driving rapid growth in new sub-segments like clean energy, functional energy, and adaptogenic blends. "Consumers, especially Gen Z and Millennial women, are reimagining energy," says Toni Shelton, VP Brand and Strategy at Collective Arts. "They're done with the 'slam a can and brace yourself' mentality. They want steady, supportive energy that fits into a balanced, wellness-focused lifestyle. Botany brings that to life with clean, adaptogenic formulations built for daily energy that fits women's lives, not the other way around." Botany Energy is part of the Botany lineup of beverages that champion the nourishment that nature intended. Botany Energy has two sister portfolios: Botany Elixirs and Botany Waters - already in market - both derived from the same values as Botany Energy but with a different set of features and functions. Botany Energy is now available in 7-Eleven stores across Canada, with expanded distribution rolling out in 2026. Botany's Elixirs and Waters can be found at select quality grocery retailers including Whole Foods, Healthy Planet, Sobey's, Fortinos and Well.ca. All Botany beverages can also be purchased in Ontario at Collective Arts Hamilton and Toronto spaces and online shop. About Collective Arts Collective Arts is on a mission to bring creativity into the everyday through the beverages they make and the artists they champion. Founded in 2013, Collective Arts fuses innovative beverages with the talents of emerging artists from around the world. Their goal is to create a locally relevant, globally iconic lifestyle brand, focused on providing artists with a platform to be discovered and amplified. TORONTO, May 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Starmount, Canada’s newest functional beverage company, launches its flagship adaptogenic energy drink, a clean, all-natural alternative to conventional options. Powered by clinically studied lion’s mane mushrooms and natural caffeine from the guarana plant, Starmount delivers a crisp, lightly sparkling lemon taste alongside sustained energy without artificial stimulants, crashes, or spikes. Behind Starmount are Nick and Lindsay Sutcliffe, a Canadian couple with nearly two decades of beverage industry experience, including establishing Pommies as part of Canada’s early craft cider movement in 2010. With their background in building consumer beverage brands, the duo saw a clear gap; popular drinks were packed with artificial ingredients, while functional beverages lacked flavour. They bridged that divide by crafting a delicious, functional mushroom beverage in a familiar energy format. “The energy drink category was long overdue for a reset,” says co-founder Lindsay Sutcliffe. ”Too many people have to choose between performance and peace of mind in what they drink. The reality is that most energy drinks are filled with artificial everything. We created Starmount for people who care about what they put in their bodies, require real, sustained energy, and expect great taste without compromise.” Designed for real life, Starmount’s convenient format makes it easy to take on the go, ready for the everyday moments when you need an energy boost the most. It is a drink for those looking for a way to realign their capacity, mentally and physically, without a jarring or extreme intervention. “We saw early on that functional mushrooms have the power to support focus, energy, and balance. That’s why we wanted to bring them into a format people already know and love,” says Nick, Starmount co-founder. “We believe the natural energy lift of guarana-derived caffeine perfectly complements the functional properties of lion’s mane mushrooms, creating a drink that delivers real benefits with zero compromise on taste and wellbeing.” The conventional energy drink category relies on synthetic caffeine and artificial sugars that deliver a short-lived boost followed by a sharp crash, often leaving consumers with jitters, heart palpitations, and increased anxiety. Starmount is designed to break that cycle by replacing harsh stimulants with natural functional mushroom compounds found in full-spectrum lion’s mane, including erinacines A and C and hericenone A, which have been studied for their potential to support cognitive performance and mood balance. Each serving of Starmount contains 1500 mg of dried lion’s mane mushrooms and 110 mg of natural caffeine sourced from guarana, providing a smoother, more gradual energy lift without the jolt. The result is sustained energy without the overly complex ingredient lists or earthy taste common in other functional beverages. For optimal results, Starmount should be consumed daily for at least one week. Starmount was made for people who embrace wellness as part of a fulfilling life, but not as an all-consuming mission; for people who are optimistic about their health choices but keep things practical and in balance with the rest of their lifestyle. Starting May 15, Starmount is available at drinkstarmount.com for $15.96 per four-can pack, with distribution expanding to local retailers in the months to follow. For more information, please visit https://drinkstarmount.com/. About Starmount Star

They are disrupting the coffee industry with ready-to-drink protein coffees that help you feel stronger, gain clarity, and become confident knowing you have the sustained energy to tackle your day. They have crafted their cold-brewed coffees with a balance of taste and performance. Each cold brewed coffee is combined with 20g of grass-fed protein to give you long-lasting energy. Recently, brüst has grown its distribution across the country into retail stores like Loblaws, Walmart, Whole Foods, and this summer Costco. They have seen growth into over 720 retail locations and are eclipsing their competition with faster velocity on shelf. brüst, announced today that it has partnered with FrontFundr on an equity crowdfunding to support brüst’s ambitious growth plans.  To drive company growth, brüst is raising money to increase production, build brand awareness, and expand into new retailers. They are using an innovative source of funding, equity crowdfunding, to execute this plan.        brüst has partnered with a Canadian crowdfunding platform called FrontFundr to help with this raise. Previous to FrontFundr, start-ups like brüst were restricted to friends and family or accredited investors. FrontFundr allows anyone to get involved!       “You don't need to be from an investment firm or be an experienced investor - you simply need to be a fan of brüst,” says Josh Barr, one of brüst’s co-founders. “We wanted to make our investment round accessible to those that love our product. Those who are interested can make a minimum investment of $250, which will secure common shares in brüst along with other perks (free brüst, brüst swag, and a chance to play tennis with top Canadian tennis player Denis Shapovalov) in return!” Full details of the offering can be found in the offering document at www.frontfundr.com/brust To learn more about brüst, visit www.brustbeverages.com .   Media contact: Josh Barr brüst M: 647-980-6249 E: [email protected] Ashley Conyngham Director, Marketing and Communications aconyngham [at] ledc.com This is how I can help.
